title: Action de Galois sur Teichmüller : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting, continued from p.102. K ⊂ ℂ is a number field, Γ = Gal(K̄/K), X/K is a variety, and T ⊂ X(ℂ) is a locally closed, simply connected subset. T plays the role of a 'base-point set', in the spirit of Grothendieck's later tangential/'droit chemin' base points. The points x, y lie in T and are K-rational.

The T-path and its Galois cocycle (p.102). l^T_{y,x} is the path from x to y inside T, viewed as an element of the profinite fundamental groupoid π̂_1(X_K̄; x, y). Galois transports it as ^u l^T_{y,x} = g^T_{y,x}(u) · l^T_{y,x}, with g^T_{y,x}(u) ∈ π̂_1(X, T). Let f : X' → X be finite and étale over T. Then X'_T is a finite disjoint union of copies of T, and 'T-adjacency' (lying in the same component) is an equivalence relation on points of X' over T. For x', y' in X'_T one gets the analogous cocycle g^T_{y',x'}(u) on X', with f̂(g^T_{y',x'}(u)) = g^T_{y,x}(u) (formula 54).

This page.
- For each connected component T_α of X'_T there is a map φ̂_α : π̂_1(X'_K̄, T_α) → π̂_1(X, T).
- If X' is a finite étale cover of X, this map is injective. Its images are the conjugate open subgroups, namely the stabilizers in π = π̂_1(X, T) of the points of the fibre π-set E = π_0(X'_T). The margin says exactly this: X' corresponds to the π-set E.
- From (54) one gets the condition: for all u ∈ Γ, g^T_{y,x}(u) ∈ ∩_{α ∈ π_0(X'_T)} Im φ̂_α. This intersection is the normal core, i.e. the kernel of π̂ → Aut(E).
- This is an arithmetic condition, necessary for the topological finite cover X' → X to come from a K-scheme structure. That structure must make f étale over K and satisfy, for every α and every u ∈ Γ, that u(x'_α) and u(y'_α) are T-adjacent. Here x'_α, y'_α are the points of the component T_α over x and y.
- Grothendieck stresses this is much weaker than requiring x', y' to be K-rational, i.e. fixed by Γ.

Why it holds. Γ preserves T-adjacency of all lifts exactly when transport along the T-path commutes with the Galois action on the fibres. That means g(u) must act trivially on E, i.e. lie in the core.

The page closes this preliminary discussion. The next page opens a new 14-page section, 'Groupoïde fondamental d'une courbe tame (préliminaires à l'action de Galois)'.

The problem served: describing the Galois action on covers (dessins and Teichmüller-type towers) through the cocycle attached to a canonical 'horizontal' path. In the case X = P^1 − {0,1,∞}, T = ]0,1[ this cocycle is the Ihara/Drinfeld f_σ ∈ F̂_2.
errors: The condition is stated as 'necessary'. Once a K-model of X' is given, it is in fact equivalent to the adjacency-preservation property. It is not sufficient for the existence of a K-model, and the text rightly keeps it as only necessary in that sense.
Notation slip: the source group is written π̂_1(X'_T, T_α). In the image the subscript is crossed out; it should be π̂_1(X'_K̄, T_α) (or π̂_1(X', T_α)).

ideas.what: Galois cocycle measuring the deviation of a canonical topological path between rational points (or a base-point set T) from Galois invariance: ^u l = g(u) l
ideas.modern_name: Ihara–Drinfeld cocycle f_σ / Galois action on étale path torsors with tangential base points
ideas.usually_credited_to: Ihara (1985–), Deligne (1989, tangential base points), Drinfeld (1990), Anderson
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (1984) only alludes to the Galois action on π̂_1 of P^1 − 3 points and Teichmüller towers; this explicit cocycle is not written there

ideas.what: Criterion: Galois preserves T-adjacency of the lifts in a cover iff the cocycle lies in the core (the intersection of the conjugate stabilizers) of the corresponding open subgroup
ideas.modern_name: Galois action on dessins d'enfants / fields of definition of covers via f_σ acting on the monodromy π-set
ideas.usually_credited_to: Folklore in dessins theory (Ihara, Schneps, Lochak, etc., 1990s)

ideas.what: A finite étale cover corresponds to a π-set E = π_0(X'_T), and the images of the component groups are the point stabilizers
ideas.modern_name: Galois correspondence for the fundamental groupoid with a set of base points (SGA1)

deep.surprise_reason: This is an early, explicit form of the Ihara/Drinfeld-type cocycle for a simply connected base-point set T, together with a simple 'core' criterion for the Galois action on covers. It is historically nice as evidence that Grothendieck worked this out around 1978–81, before Ihara's and Drinfeld's publications. Mathematically, however, it is routine and is now standard in the dessins/GT literature.
transcription_corrections: 'π̂_1(X'_{T}, T_α)': in the image the subscript is crossed out; read π̂_1(X'_{K̄}, T_α).
'[?] Γ4 [?]' is most likely 'la formule (54) donne' — i.e. 'Donc la formule (54) [donne] la condition ...'.
'la condition nécessaire et suffisante' reads more like '(*) la condition entièrement [?]'; the text itself afterwards calls it 'une condition arithmétique, nécessaire'.

Marginal note (oblique), plausible reading: 'Si X' est un rev. étale de X, l'on sait que X' est défini par un π-ensemble E = π_0(X'_T), avec π = π_1(X,T) ... Γ opère sur π̂ ... la 2e condition dit que ... π → Aut(E)'.
The final parenthetical reads '(ce qui est une condition nettement plus faible que celle que x', y' ∈ X'_K i.e. x', y' fixes sous Γ)'.
